module_level_findings.finding: Machenschaft → Gestell is not a synonym chain
module_level_findings.detail: Machenschaft is a late-1930s history-of-being interpretation of makeability/objectifiability; Gestell is a later ordering/revealing diagnosis. Their relation is reconstructive and must be bridged, not presumed.
A totalizing Gestell claim is methodologically weak if every modern technology counts by definition. The module requires concrete ordering signatures and counterdescriptions.

module_level_findings.finding: Bestand is contextual resourceization, not simple object identity
module_level_findings.detail: Availability, substitutability and chained demand can organize an artifact/person as standing-reserve within a system while alternative descriptions/practices remain possible.
GA7 says the human never becomes merely Bestand; GA79 says the human can be a Bestand-Stück in a distinctive way. The profile preserves the tension rather than flattening it.

module_level_findings.finding: Concrete technology requires native design/governance analysis
module_level_findings.detail: Current philosophy of technology treats technology as heterogeneous design/artifact/sociotechnical practice. Multi-criteria design, lifecycle governance and responsibility structures can instantiate some ordering pressures without proving a single total technological essence.

module_level_findings.finding: Late technology diagnosis must not erase corrigibility
module_level_findings.detail: Contemporary governance and responsibility frameworks show that technical systems can contain review, human oversight and correction channels. These do not refute Heidegger, but force a more discriminating Gestell claim.
